paragraphs: ImageTrend sells software that fire departments, EMS agencies, and hospitals run their emergency response operations on. Its core product is ePCR software built for how medics actually work, with AI-assisted documentation, configurable workflows, and real-time intelligence for agencies at any scale.

The platform connects scheduling, documentation, compliance, unified analytics, operational readiness, and hospital data exchange in one system. NEMSIS, NERIS, NTDB, and TQIP compliance is built into every workflow, with software filling and validating fields while staff review and confirm before submission. A scheduling product, ImageTrend Slate, addresses the demands of EMS, fire departments, and other critical services. It manages time-off requests, shift trades, and employee availability. Separate pre-plan software digitizes floor plans, hazard locations, water supply points, and utility shutoffs so responders have instant access to tactical data on scene.

The company reports 9,000 agencies, 43 state repositories, and more than a billion records processed. It says its sales engineering team is entirely former fire and EMS. It cites 24/7 US-based support and a 96.5% satisfaction rate, backed by 25 years in the field.

quote.text: Other vendors build software and ask you to fit your operation around it.
